taxonomy.reference: Kitchener A.C. et al. (2017). A revised taxonomy of the Felidae: The final report of the Cat Classification Task Force of the IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group. Cat News Special Issue 11.
taxonomy.taxonomy_note: The 41 recognised extant felid species comprise 40 wild species plus the domestic cat (Felis catus). This follows the 2017 CatSG revision; it is a documented snapshot, not a permanent universal constant.

breed_registry.name: Cat Fanciers' Association (CFA)
breed_registry.verification: Each breed profile URL was fetched and its page title checked on 2026-10-25.
breed_registry.note: TICA and FIFe recognise partly different breed lists. FelidLens uses CFA as the single documented registry for this catalogue.

taxonomy.breed_note: Breed names are not scientific taxa. Every breed is assigned to Felis catus and excluded from species counts.
taxonomy.hybrid_note: Hybrids are listed separately for completeness and are excluded from species and breed counts.

species.description: The lion is a large felid native to Africa and India. Muscular and broad-chested with a tufted tail, adult males possess a magnificent dark mane. It is the only truly social wild cat, living in structured family prides.
distinguishing_characteristics: Prominent mane in adult males
Tawny yellow-gold unspotted coat in adults
Black brush tuft at tail tip
Social pride structure of related females and a coalition of males
species.geographic_range: Sub-Saharan Africa; Gir National Park in Gujarat, Western India
species.diet: Apex obligate carnivore; primarily large ungulates (wildebeest, zebras, buffalo)
species.behavior: Social pride living; mostly nocturnal and crepuscular hunting; roaring audible up to 8 km.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Giles Laurent / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Cougars have a smaller, sleeker head, no mane, white muzzle ring, and purr rather than roar.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The tiger is the largest living cat species. Recognizable for its dark vertical stripes on reddish-orange fur with white underbellies. Solitary apex predators with an affinity for water and swimming.
distinguishing_characteristics: Distinctive vertical black stripes unique to every individual
Reddish-orange coat with white ventral coloration
Prominent white spot ('ocellus') on the back of each ear
Superior swimming and aquatic ambush capabilities
species.size_and_weight: Total length: up to 310 cm; Weight: 90-300 kg depending on subspecies
species.geographic_range: South Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Russian Far East
species.diet: Large ungulates including deer (sambar, chital), wild boar, and wild cattle
species.behavior: Solitary and territorial; patrol large home ranges; frequently bathes in rivers.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Charles J. Sharp / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The jaguar is the only extant Panthera species native to the Americas. Muscular and stocky, it possesses the most crushing bite force relative to body size of all cats, puncturing turtle carapaces with ease.
distinguishing_characteristics: Large rosette patterns containing central black spots
Exceptionally compact, muscular build with broad head and thick jaw
Direct cranial bite strategy piercing temporal skull bones
Strong affinity for swimming in rivers and swamps
species.size_and_weight: Head-body: 112-185 cm; Weight: 56-96 kg (exceptional males exceed 140 kg)
species.geographic_range: Southwestern US borderlands through Central America to the Pantanal and Amazon
species.diet: Broad generalist: caiman, capybaras, tapirs, turtles, and peccaries
species.behavior: Solitary apex predator; stalk-and-ambush hunter; adept swimmer.
species.image_attribution: Photo: USFWS / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

similar_species.differentiator: Leopard rosettes lack interior black spots and leopards have longer, leaner frames.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The leopard is famous for its supreme agility, stealth, and arboreal strength. It hoists carcasses heavier than its own body high into tree branches to protect them from hyenas and lions.
distinguishing_characteristics: Dense rosettes with hollow, spot-free centers
Slender athletic build with long balancing tail (60-100 cm)
Master of climbing; rests and caches food aloft
Frequent melanistic ('black panther') morphs in humid tropical zones
species.geographic_range: Sub-Saharan Africa, Middle East, Central Asia, India, and China
species.diet: Opportunistic: antelopes, deer, baboons, and wild pigs
species.behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; caches prey in tree forks.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Sumeet Moghe / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Cheetahs have solid round spots, facial tear marks, and tall slender builds.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The 'Ghost of the Mountains' roams the high peaks of Central Asia. Perfectly adapted to alpine conditions with thick smoky fur, broad snowshoe paws, and an enormous tail wrapped around its face for warmth.
distinguishing_characteristics: Thick smoky-grey fur with muted black rosettes
Exceptionally long, plush tail (80-105 cm) used as balance and muffler
Fur-covered footpads providing snow traction
Large nasal cavity warming frigid thin air before lung entry
species.geographic_range: High mountains of Central and South Asia (Himalayas, Tien Shan, Altai)
species.diet: Mountain ungulates (blue sheep/bharal, ibex, markhor) and marmots
species.behavior: Solitary cliff stalker; leaps up to 15 meters; non-roaring vocal anatomy.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Irbis1983 / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: A canopy specialist of Southeast Asian rainforests. It has the longest canines in proportion to skull size of any living carnivore and can climb down tree trunks headfirst like a squirrel.
distinguishing_characteristics: Enormous canine teeth relative to head size (up to 4 cm)
Large cloud-shaped irregular dark blotches
Reversible ankle joints allowing head-first vertical descent
Extremely long balancing tail and wide stabilizing paws
species.geographic_range: Southeast Asia, southern China, eastern Himalayas
species.diet: Primates (gibbons, macaques), deer, and wild pigs
species.behavior: Arboreal hunter; drops from branches onto terrestrial prey; nocturnal.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Rushenb / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Native to Borneo and Sumatra, genetically distinct from the mainland clouded leopard. It features smaller, darker cloud markings with distinctive central spots inside the clouds.
distinguishing_characteristics: Darker overall pelage with smaller cloud blotches containing inner spots
Proportionately huge canines and muscular arboreal limbs
Heavy double dorsal stripe running along back
Strictly restricted to the Sunda islands of Borneo and Sumatra
species.geographic_range: Islands of Borneo and Sumatra (Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei)
species.diet: Sambar deer, mouse deer, bearded pigs, proboscis monkeys
species.behavior: Canopy predator; highly elusive; threatened by palm oil deforestation.
species.image_attribution: Photo: www.photosbypaulo.com / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Mainland clouded leopards are lighter yellow-tawny with larger, cleaner cloud markings.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: A medium-sized forest cat of Southeast Asia exhibiting polymorphic coloration ranging from golden-red and dark brown to spotted and melanistic phases. Known for conspicuous white facial lines.
distinguishing_characteristics: Conspicuous white lines flanked by dark brown stripes extending from inner eye corners upward
Tail tip underside is conspicuously whitish and carried curled upward
Solid golden, chestnut, or grey coat phase ('golden cat')
Powerful stocky limbs adapted to mountain forests
species.geographic_range: Northeast India, Bhutan, Southeast Asia, southern China, Sumatra
species.diet: Muntjacs (barking deer), wild pigs, mouse deer, and ground birds
species.behavior: Both terrestrial and arboreal hunter; solitary; marks trails with urine and scent.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Karen Stout / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.conservation_title: Endangered (One of the world's most elusive cats)
species.description: Endemic exclusively to the island of Borneo. Characterized by its chestnut-red or slate-grey coat, long tapering tail with a pale underside, and rounded head with short ears.
distinguishing_characteristics: Endemic strictly to Borneo island
Long tail tapering toward tip with distinctive white ventral line
Small rounded ears set low on the skull
Extremely low camera-trap detection rates; fewer than 2,500 remain
species.size_and_weight: Head-body: 53-67 cm; Tail: 32-39 cm; Weight: 3-4 kg
species.geographic_range: Endemic to the island of Borneo (Indonesia & Malaysia)
species.diet: Small forest rodents, birds, and lizards
species.behavior: Extremely secretive forest specialist; primarily nocturnal; severely threatened by logging.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Jim Sanderson derivative work: Abujoy / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The marbled cat looks like a miniature clouded leopard, with marbled blotches and an extraordinarily long, bushy tail longer than its head-body length used to balance aloft in canopy vines.
distinguishing_characteristics: Bushy tail exceeding the length of its head and body (up to 55 cm)
Irregular clouded marbled patches with thick dark borders
Flexible limbs with broad paws designed for canopy locomotion
Miniature build weighing only 2-5 kg
species.size_and_weight: Head-body: 45-62 cm; Tail: 35-55 cm; Weight: 2-5 kg
species.geographic_range: Eastern Himalayas through Southeast Asia, Sumatra, and Borneo
species.diet: Arboreal rodents, squirrels, tree birds, and bats
species.behavior: Almost exclusively arboreal and crepuscular; acrobatic forest canopy dweller.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Johan Embréus (Embreus ) / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Clouded leopards are four times heavier with massive canines and shorter relative tails.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Characterized by long black ear tufts and an unspotted tawny-red coat. Known for its acrobatic vertical jumps snatching birds out of mid-air up to 3 meters above the ground.
distinguishing_characteristics: Extremely long black ear tufts exceeding 4.5 cm
Uniform reddish-tawny coat without torso spotting
20 individual ear muscles directing auditory radar
Astounding aerial leaping ability catching flying gamebirds
species.geographic_range: Africa, Middle East, Central Asia, and northwestern India
species.diet: Guineafowl, francolins, hares, rodents, and small antelopes
species.behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; marks territory with scent and claw markings.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Derek Keats / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Servals are heavily spotted with round dish-like ears; caracals are unspotted with tufted ears.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Endemic to the equatorial rainforests of Central and West Africa. Exhibiting rich golden-red to slate-grey coloration, it is twice the size of a domestic cat and closely related to the caracal.
distinguishing_characteristics: Rounded head with small ears lacking long caracal-style tufts
Coat varies from bright reddish-gold to silver-grey or chocolate
Variable spotting, often prominent on belly and inner legs
Specialized inhabitant of the Congo Basin tropical forests
species.geographic_range: Equatorial rainforest belt of Central and West Africa (Congo Basin)
species.diet: Forest duikers, giant pouched rats, monkeys, and tree pangolins
species.behavior: Secretive terrestrial stalker; rarely observed directly; threatened by bushmeat hunting.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Greco & Rovero / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Has the longest legs and biggest ears relative to body size of any cat. These acoustic radar adaptations allow it to pinpoint burrowing rodents beneath savanna reeds and pounce in high parabolic arcs.
distinguishing_characteristics: Disproportionately long, slender stilting legs
Enormous upright oval ears set closely together
Golden coat with bold black spots merging into neck bars
High arching vertical pounce with >50% hunting success
species.size_and_weight: Head-body: 59-100 cm; Shoulder height: 54-62 cm; Weight: 7-18 kg
species.geographic_range: Sub-Saharan Africa, centered on well-watered savanna wetlands
species.diet: Small rodents (vlei rats), birds, frogs, and lizards
species.behavior: Auditory hunter; stalks through tall grass; solitary.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Diego Delso / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Caracals have pointed tufted ears and uniform unspotted red coats.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Medium-sized neotropical spotted cat ranging from southern Texas to northern Argentina. Marked with longitudinal chains of elongated rosettes and parallel cheek stripes.
distinguishing_characteristics: Chains of dark-bordered elongated spots running in lines down the body
Prominent white spot ('ocellus') on back of each ear
Muscular body weighing 8-16 kg
Reversible ankle joints for tree climbing
species.geographic_range: Southern Texas through Central America to Northern Argentina
species.diet: Opossums, armadillos, rodents, birds, and iguanas
species.behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; maintains scent-sprayed pathways.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Giles Laurent / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Margays are half the size with proportionally giant eyes and longer tails.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The supreme acrobat of the cat family. Its hind ankles can rotate 180 degrees, allowing it to run vertically down tree trunks headfirst and hang from branches by a single foot.
distinguishing_characteristics: Enormous nocturnal eyes adapted for rainforest canopy depth perception
Hind ankles rotate 180° inward for acrobatic tree navigation
Extremely long tail (70% of head-body length) for balance
Vocal mimicry of prey species (e.g. pied tamarin infants)
species.size_and_weight: Head-body: 48-79 cm; Tail: 33-51 cm; Weight: 2.6-4 kg
species.geographic_range: Mexico through Central America to northern Argentina and Uruguay
species.diet: Canopy rodents, squirrels, tree frogs, fruit, and small birds
species.behavior: Strictly arboreal and nocturnal; lives life in high canopy branches.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Supreet Sahoo / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Ocelots are much heavier with smaller relative eye diameters.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: One of the rarest, most endangered felids in existence. Surviving only on barren, freezing Andean slopes above 3,500 meters, it preys almost exclusively on mountain viscachas.
distinguishing_characteristics: Thick cylindrical tail with 6-9 dark brown rings, almost as long as body
Ash-grey plush coat with orange-brown vertical flank bars
Strictly restricted to high rocky scree in the Andes (>3,500 m)
Specialized predator of chinchillas and mountain viscachas
species.size_and_weight: Head-body: 57-64 cm; Tail: 41-48 cm; Weight: 4-5 kg
species.geographic_range: High Andes of Peru, Bolivia, northern Chile, and northwest Argentina
species.diet: Mountain viscachas (Lagidium viscacia) and high-elevation rodents
species.behavior: Solitary scree climber; counterbalances rapid leaps with thick tail.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Jim Sanderson / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The smallest wild cat in the Americas, weighing only 1.5-3 kg. Native to the temperate Valdivian rainforests of Chile and adjacent Argentina, it has a tiny face, bushy ringed tail, and black spots.
distinguishing_characteristics: Smallest felid in the Western Hemisphere (1.5-3 kg)
Brownish-yellow coat densely covered in small round black spots
Bushy tail with 10-12 dark rings
High rate of melanism (pure black morphs common)
species.geographic_range: Central and southern Chile, western border of Argentina
species.diet: Small forest rodents, thrushes, chucao tapaculos, lizards
species.behavior: Agile climber; nests in tree hollows; threatened by forest fragmentation.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Mauro Tammone / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Native to the southern half of South America. About the size of a domestic cat, covered in countless small black spots, and renowned for frequently standing upright on its hind legs to survey surroundings.
distinguishing_characteristics: Regularly stands upright on hind legs ('tripod stance') to peer over tall grass
Numerous small, clearly separated black spots over silvery-ochre coat
Excellent swimmer that readily enters wetlands for fish and frogs
Dark cheek lines and prominent white ear patches
species.geographic_range: Pampas and Gran Chaco of Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay
species.diet: Hares, rodents, marsh birds, fish, and frogs
species.behavior: Solitary and nocturnal; uses tree crotches as latrines and resting sites.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Daf-de / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.5)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The largest of the four lynx species and third largest European predator. Characterized by long black ear tufts, flared facial ruff, powerful hindquarters, and huge snowshoe paws.
distinguishing_characteristics: Prominent 4 cm black ear tufts acting as acoustic aids
Short bobbed tail ending in a completely black tip
Wide facial ruff framing the jaw
Furred, webbed paws distributing weight across deep winter snow
species.geographic_range: Northern and Eastern Europe, Siberia, and Central Asia
species.diet: Medium-sized ungulates (roe deer, chamois) and mountain hares
species.behavior: Solitary stalker; exceptional sight and hearing; patrols vast home ranges.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Aconcagua / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Canada lynx are smaller (8-14 kg) with silver coats and even bigger snowshoe paws.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Adaptable North American predator ranging from southern Canada to central Mexico. Named for its stubby bobbed tail, which uniquely features a bright white underside at the tip.
distinguishing_characteristics: Tail tip is black on dorsal side but clear bright white underneath
Reddish-brown to grey-brown pelage with dark bar markings on forelimbs
Moderate black ear tufts shorter than Canadian lynx
White eye circles and white ear spots
species.geographic_range: North America from southern Canada throughout the US to central Mexico
species.diet: Cottontail rabbits, hares, rodents, birds, and young ungulates
species.behavior: Crepuscular and territorial; agile climber and swimmer.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Becker1999 (Paul and Cathy) / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Canada lynx tails are solid black all around the tip with no white underside.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Specialized boreal hunter whose population numbers fluctuate in tandem with the 10-year abundance cycle of snowshoe hares. Has enormous snowshoe paws with low foot loading.
distinguishing_characteristics: Tail tip is entirely black on all sides
Huge fur-padded paws creating low pressure on powder snow
Very long ear tufts (>3.5 cm) and flared beard ruff
Silvery-grey thick winter fur with faint markings
species.geographic_range: Boreal forests of Canada and Alaska, northern tier of US states
species.diet: Snowshoe hares (75-97% of diet), grouse, and red squirrels
species.behavior: Crepuscular and nocturnal; travels silently through deep snow.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Michael Zahra / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The world's most threatened felid in 2002, now recovering in Spain and Portugal thanks to historic reintroduction initiatives. Features heavy leopard-like spots and a rabbit-dependent diet.
distinguishing_characteristics: Intensely spotted coat with crisp, dark, leopard-like markings
Long pointed ear tufts and pronounced dual-pointed facial beard
Strict dietary dependence on European wild rabbits (>80%)
Endemic to Mediterranean maquis scrub of Spain and Portugal
species.geographic_range: Iberian Peninsula (Andalusia, Castilla-La Mancha, Extremadura, Alentejo)
species.diet: European wild rabbits (Oryctolagus cunicuniculus)
species.behavior: Solitary territorial predator; European rewilding flagship.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Diego Delso / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: The fastest terrestrial mammal, capable of bursts up to 112 km/h (70 mph). Evolutionarily specialized with semi-retractile claws for traction, deep chest, and dark facial tear lines.
distinguishing_characteristics: Black tear stripes from eye corners to mouth to reduce solar glare
Solid small round black spots over golden fur
Semi-retractile claws functioning like track sprint spikes
Deep chest and flexible spine enabling massive sprinting strides
species.geographic_range: Eastern and Southern Africa; relict Asiatic cheetah population in Iran
species.diet: Medium ungulates (Thomson's gazelle, impala, springbok) and hares
species.behavior: Diurnal hunter avoiding larger nocturnal carnivores; high-speed sprint chase.
species.image_attribution: Photo: AfricanConservation / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Leopards are stocky with rosettes; cheetahs have solid dots and tear stripes.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Holds the record for the broadest latitudinal range of any native terrestrial mammal in the Western Hemisphere, stretching from northern Yukon to Patagonia. A large, solitary purring cat.
distinguishing_characteristics: Tawny-beige unspotted coat with white muzzle ring and black whisker spots
Cylindrical tail with prominent dark black tip
Massive hind legs powering vertical leaps of up to 5.5 meters
Purring felid; lacks hyoid elasticity required to roar
species.geographic_range: Western Canada and US through Central and South America to Tierra del Fuego
species.diet: Deer (mule deer, white-tailed deer), elk, bighorn sheep, and smaller mammals
species.behavior: Solitary ambush hunter; caches kills under brush and snow.
species.image_attribution: Photo: National Park Service / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

similar_species.differentiator: Lions have much larger skulls, male manes, pride lifestyle, and roar.

species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: An unusual neotropical cat with an otter-like body, short limbs, small flattened head, and unspotted coat occurring in grey and red color morphs. Predominantly active by day.
distinguishing_characteristics: Otter-like low elongated silhouette with short legs and long tail
Unspotted coat in two morphs: dark charcoal-grey and bright red-chestnut
Strictly diurnal (daytime hunter)
Unusual vocal repertoire of 13 vocalizations including bird-like chirps
species.geographic_range: Central America and South America to central Argentina
species.diet: Ground birds (chachalacas), rodents, snakes, and lizards
species.behavior: Diurnal ground stalker; moves through dense brush; highly vocal.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Vassil / Wikimedia Commons (CC0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Adapted to the high-altitude, freezing steppes of Central Asia. Possesses the densest fur of any felid, low-set ears allowing it to peer over rock edges without being seen, and unique round pupils.
distinguishing_characteristics: Low-set, widely spaced rounded ears on the sides of the flat head
Circular pupils that contract into round dots rather than vertical slits
Plush, frosted silvery coat protecting against subzero temperatures
Short, heavily furred black-tipped tail
species.geographic_range: Central Asian steppes (Mongolia, Tibetan Plateau, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan)
species.diet: Pikas, voles, small ground birds, and insects
species.behavior: Ambush hunter in rocky outcrops; low profile stalking; solitary.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Sander van der Wel / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: Small spotted wild cat widespread across South, Southeast, and East Asia. Wild progenitor of the modern domestic Bengal cat breed. An agile climber and capable swimmer.
distinguishing_characteristics: Two conspicuous dark facial stripes running up from forehead to nape
Yellow-ochre coat patterned with black rosettes and spots
White muzzle, chin, and throat
Adept swimmer and agile climber
species.geographic_range: Widespread across Asia from India to China, Korea, and Russian Far East
species.diet: Murid rodents, bats, small birds, reptiles, and amphibians
species.behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; often frequents oil palm and agricultural boundaries.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Abujoy / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
species.taxonomy_source: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

provenance.taxonomy: IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group (Kitchener et al. 2017)

species.description: A semiaquatic wetland specialist in South and Southeast Asia. Features partially webbed front paws, water-resistant double coat, and a habit of diving underwater to catch fish.
distinguishing_characteristics: Partially webbed front paws powering aquatic propulsion
Dense water-resistant undercoat preventing skin saturation
Strong rudder-like muscular tail
Taps water surfaces to mimic insects and draw fish within strike reach
species.geographic_range: Disjunct wetlands of South and Southeast Asia (India, Sri Lanka, Thailand)
species.diet: Fish (>75% of diet), crabs, water snakes, mollusks, and frogs
species.behavior: Semiaquatic hunter; swims long distances; predominantly nocturnal.
species.image_attribution: Photo: Kelinahandbasket / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

Muted grey-brown coat without white mittens or patches
Significantly wider skull and brain volume than domestic cats
Secretive woodland habit avoiding human settlements

Broad flat head with large, wide-set triangular ears detecting underground sound
Sandy-buff coloration providing total camouflage among desert dunes
Can survive indefinitely without open drinking water, deriving moisture from prey

species.diet: Desert rodents (gerbils, spiny mice), desert lizards, vipers, and insects

species.description: Africa's smallest wild cat and biologically the world's deadliest feline with an unprecedented 60% hunting success rate. Makes a kill every 50 minutes throughout the night to sustain its high metabolism.

species.description: The oncilla, also called the northern tiger cat, is a small spotted cat of Central America and the Amazon basin. Its slender build, narrow muzzle and open rosettes separate it from the larger ocelot, while genetic work continues to revise the boundaries of the Leopardus tigrinus complex.
distinguishing_characteristics: Small, slender build with a narrow muzzle and long tail
Open black rosettes on a tawny to ochre ground colour
Two dark bands across the chest and sides of the neck
Nocturnal and partly arboreal, using trees for rest and hunting
species.size_and_weight: Head-body: 38-59 cm; Tail: 20-42 cm; Weight: 1.5-3 kg
species.geographic_range: Disjunct populations in Costa Rica and Panama; Amazon basin and Cerrado of northern and central Brazil
species.diet: Small rodents, lizards, birds, tree frogs, and insects
species.behavior: Nocturnal and crepuscular; solitary and agile in trees; often rests in dense cover.

species.description: The southern tigrina is a small spotted cat of the Atlantic Forest and adjacent savannas in southern Brazil, Paraguay and northeastern Argentina. It was separated from the oncilla on genetic evidence and is extremely difficult to tell apart by coat alone.

Slightly darker and larger-rosetted than the oncilla, with a shorter tail
Adults weigh roughly 1.9-2.4 kg
Inhabits dense tropical and subtropical forest as well as open savanna

species.description: The Pampas cat is a small, thick-furred wild cat of South American grasslands, shrublands and Andean slopes. Its coat varies strongly across its range, but all forms show two dark cheek lines and a bushy, ringed tail.

Highly variable pelage, from spotted to almost plain
